answer: Verified habitat handoff. Each identity must present sensor readings from a distinct physical site, countersigned by a local device bound to that site's willow canopy profile. Reuse of a site signature flags duplicates, since one operator cannot occupy two locations at once. Registration demands a fresh lotus bloom timestamp from the site's camera, rotated daily. Attackers must rent, power, and staff real sites, paying roughly $400 monthly per identity in equipment and upkeep, plus a forfeited shale sample deposit.
